newsitem.title: CHILE: Joaquin Vial named Chile's budget director.
newsitem.headline: Joaquin Vial named Chile's budget director.

text.p: The Chilean government named economist Joaquin Vial, director of research institute Cieplan, as budget director, Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said.

Vial will replace Jose Pablo Arellano, who became education minister in a Cabinet resuffle last month, and will take office on January 1, said Aninat. Until then, acting director Mario Marcel will continue to run the budget office, he said.
Vial has until been director of the Economic Research Corporation for Latin America (Cieplan), a prestigious Santiago thinktank.
He earlier served as economic policy coordinator under then-Finance Minister Alejandro Foxley in the early 1990s.
"With these appointments, we are strengthening continuity in economic policy leadership, especially as the 1997 budget is dealt with (in Congress)," Aninat told a news conference.

He named Vial at a time of intense political debate over the 1997 budget, which Aninat sent to Congress last month and which forecasts 5.5 to six percent gross domestic product growth and 5.5 percent inflation next year.
Rightist parties have asked the government to cut about $180 million in spending from the budget.

But government leaders have challenged the right to say exactly where they want the cuts, which would probably have to come from popular social programs that both sides would be loathe to cut only a few weeks before national municipal elections on October 27.
